thread:
carmen: Heads-up: AZ3 maintenance tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. We'll push NIC microcode + spine switch firmware. Plan is to do 3 cohorts (rack groups) with staggered host reboots. Expected impact: ~6-10% GPU capacity reduction per cohort for ~10-15m during the reboot, plus transient egress latency spikes.
sam: Timeline and canary details?
carmen: Canary = 2 hosts in cohort A at 02:00. If OK for 20m, continue with cohort B then C. Full plan on the runbook: https://console.redwood.internal/d/az3-maint  — includes rollback steps and traffic steering.
kevin: Can we route burst traffic to eu-west1/us-east1 during the window? How much lead time to spin up preemptible backfill?
carmen: Yes. We have a prewarm script that can provision preemptible GPU nodes in us-east in ~8-12 minutes. If we decide to backfill we'll start prewarm at 01:45. Cost is roughly 0.6x regular for preemptible, ballpark $2.4/hr per GPU (depends on SKU).
nora: Need to confirm KV-cache reseed behavior — do we preserve prefix caches across the reboot? If not we'll see a cold-cache hit and token cost bump.
kevin: We should prime the KV cache on cohort B/C after reboot. Suggest running the seed job immediately after node readiness.
carmen: Agreed. Seed job will run automatically via orchestration hook (jobs/kv-seed -> seed-cohort.sh). Putting the snippet here for ops: 
```bash
# cordon -> drain -> reboot -> uncordon
kubectl cordon node-az3-01
kubectl drain node-az3-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
ssh ops@node-az3-01 sudo reboot
# post-reboot
kubectl uncordon node-az3-01
```
sam: SRE: please add a temporary alert suppression for the latency burst (we get pager churn otherwise). Also lower autoscaler sensitivity so we don't autoscale down during the momentary spike.
nora: I'll add a muted alert window 01:50-04:20 for the maintenance tags. Also bump the healthcheck threshold to avoid eviction storms.
infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance ticket INFRA-8132 created and linked. Notifying customers in the 24h channel.
kevin: One more ask: add a firewall fallback route for egress to avoid transient SNAT exhaustion. Last time we saw port depletion for heavy multi-tenant jobs.
carmen: Good call — will add egress NAT pool expansion + short-lived connection reuse knob. Plan updated in runbook.
sam: :thumbsup: If the canary fails, what's the rollback?
carmen: Rollback = halt cohort progression, reapply previous NIC firmware on canary hosts, and schedule follow-up during low-traffic window. We also have an automatic traffic shift back to other regions via routing policy: route-policy az3-fallback -> eu-west1.
kevin: I'll monitor cost while backfilling; ping me if we cross $500/hr in burst.
nora: Post-mortem owner assigned: nora. Will collect KV-seed timing and customer-impact metrics.
carmen: Thanks all. Quick checklist for oncall: 1) prewarm if needed at 01:45, 2) run canary at 02:00, 3) watch dashboard https://console.redwood.internal/d/az3-maint and the token-cost panel, 4) abort on >10% sustained error rate for 10m.
sam: Acknowledged. I'll be on-call during the window.
kevin: I'll standby for backfill and firewall tweak.
ora: I'll own the alert suppression and postmortem.
infra-bot: Reminder: maintenance starts in 18 hours.
